source.title: Non-contact surface roughness evaluation of milling surface using CNN-deep learning models

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper; no relevant truncation or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out image-classification performance, extending the optimizer comparison to machined-surface images and a task-specific CNN.
record.gate_note: The study compares four optimizers on a CNN trained to classify surface-roughness images. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolution versus fully connected architecture, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive optimizers with SGD using held-out accuracy on a new image-classification task, bearing on V4. Reported models use fixed, untuned optimizer configurations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that RAdam performed best and that the CNN classified surface roughness accurately. Their conclusion section incorrectly calls 93.31% test accuracy; Section 6.3 identifies it as validation accuracy and reports test accuracy of 92.91%.
record.recipe_differences: Task-specific machined-surface image classification with one CNN; four optimizers were compared, but the study does not use the original claim's benchmarks or report the cited broader optimizer comparisons. Optimizer hyperparameters were specified separately; reported models were not hyperparameter tuned.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice and training duration affected performance; the text reports RAdam best and degradation after 30 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Reported optimizers exceed 90% accuracy; longer training generally degrades performance, which the authors attribute to overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training duration affects held-out performance on surface-roughness classification.

record.peer_reviewed: International Journal of Computer Integrated Manufacturing (Print), venue stated in supplied metadata
record.problems: No random-label or memorization-capacity test. Per-optimizer performance values are presented in figures without numeric values in the text; training was run three times at 10, 20, and 30 epochs, but variability is not reported. One optimizer, rmsProp, was excluded from reported results because of poor performance. Hyperparameters were not tuned for the reported models.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Learning-rate and schedule tuning comparable to the original experiments; matched training performance; language tasks; whether broader tuning changes optimizer rankings; AdamW versus coupled weight decay; and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: RMSProp was also tested and omitted because of poor performance. Record this qualitative outcome with its comparison to SGD undetermined; the reported ranking covers only the four retained optimizers.

record.verdict_notes: The reversed ranking challenges the disadvantage in this tested setting, not the frequency claim across benchmarks. No uncertainty or readable per-optimizer numerical differences are supplied. The provided text is a 2021 preprint with DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-246947/v1, rather than text explicitly identified with the record's 2022 journal DOI.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected models and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Large-batch comparison and batch-size-dependent generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: Compared performance over training durations; text reports accuracy above 90% for all four optimizers.
rows.value: All four presented optimizers showed accuracy over 90%, regardless of epoch; 10 epochs resulted in better performance, while 30 epochs degraded performance.
rows.note: The text does not give per-optimizer accuracy values here. It attributes 30-epoch degradation to overfitting.
rows.check: Absolute accuracy above 90% and degradation with longer training do not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD difference. The aggregate also obscures the separately reported, non-significant improvement of AdamW with increasing epochs.

relationships.condition: Task-specific surface-image CNN, reported untuned configurations, 10–30 epochs, SGD without momentum
relationships.reason: The text explicitly ranks RAdam, AdamW, and Adamax above SGD (R1–R4), reversing the adaptive-method disadvantage in this setting; SGD convergence difficulties limit interpretation.
relationships.display_finding: RAdam, AdamW and Adamax reportedly ranked above SGD, but the comparison remains unverified and SGD had convergence difficulties.
